args.rationale:
The recommendation to create a new purchase order for 800 units is rejected. Simulation shows that ordering 800 units is infeasible as it costs $12,000.00 from SUP-A or $14,000.00 from SUP-B, exceeding the available budget limit of $10,000.00. Furthermore, creating a new order is unnecessary because existing open order PO-505 already has 2,000 units scheduled for receipt on 2026-10-01 from SUP-A.

Under baseline conditions (1,000 usable units on hand, 100 units/day forecast demand), stock runs out on 2026-09-26 closing, resulting in 400 unmet demand units between 2026-09-27 and 2026-09-30.

Expedite simulation demonstrates that moving PO-505's receipt date forward by 4 days to 2026-09-27 eliminates the entire 400-unit shortage (reducing unmet demand to 0 units) at an incremental cost of $450.00. This action is feasible against hard budget ($10,000.00 available) and capacity (peak occupancy 60.00 m³ vs 200.00 m³ capacity) constraints. Because the $450.00 expedite fee exceeds the buyer's $250.00 autonomy limit, this plan requires buyer approval.
important_factors: The baseline projection shows usable opening inventory of 1,000 units and demand of 100 units/day, leading to a 400-unit shortage from 2026-09-27 to 2026-09-30 prior to the arrival of PO-505 on 2026-10-01.
The recommended order of 800 units is infeasible because its total cost ($12,000.00 from SUP-A or $14,000.00 from SUP-B) exceeds the available budget of $10,000.00 by $2,000.00 or $4,000.00.
Existing purchase order PO-505 for 2,000 units from SUP-A can be expedited by 4 days to arrive on 2026-09-27 for a fee of $450.00.
Expedite action completely eliminates the 400-unit stockout (total unmet units reduced to 0), leaves closing inventory at 200 units, and is feasible within the $10,000.00 available budget.
The $450.00 expedite fee exceeds the buyer autonomy limit of $250.00, requiring buyer approval.
